description.narrative: The project's overall objective is increased growth, income and employment for rural people, especially for youth, women and Roma in target markets. The specific outcomes of the project are: 1. Rural enterprises, small farmers/producers grow and provide more income and employment opportunities for the people from the rural area, women and youth in particular. 2. Local communities are resilient and sustainable, providing support in rural development especially for poor members of the communities in the selected market systems. 3. More Roma people have the capacities and the access to the job market, to take up employment and business opportunities in the selected market systems. 4. Organisational development. Outcomes one to three are directly related to Marked System Development (MSD). Outcome four is not directly linked to the MSD approach, but is believed to be crucial for achieving the programme. Moreover, the project will focus on three intervention areas: 1) The first outcome will be achieved by facilitating access to the market for companies that empower rural women and youth. 2) To achieve the second outcome, the project will focus on promoting supporting services and enabling environment (rules and regulation) for local communities. 3) The third outcome will be achieved by facilitating access to skills and access to finance for employment and self-employment of Roma people. While the areas are defined, specific interventions to be implemented within each area are not yet designed. Instead, and in line with a MSD-approach, interventions will be piloted during the inception phase with the potential to scale-up in the implementation phase. The inception phase for this programme is twelve months, April to March 2022. MSD is an approach to development that works through public and private actors to generate sustainable large-scale impact. It is analysis-led and does not prescribe or prohibit any particular instrument or tool of intervention. Instead, interventions are developed to respond to align with the capabilities and incentives of those public, private, and civil society actors, and adapted based on piloting and learning. Instead of focusing on what MSD programmes can "deliver", emphasis is placed on how systems can work better to deliver impacts for disadvantaged people.

We Effect har inkommit med en ansökan om Sidas stöd till programmet "Income Increase and Socio-Economic Empowerment of Vulnerable and Marginalised Groups from Rural and Sub-Urban Areas 2021-2023, IISEE". Ansökan avser ett treårigt stöd, 2021-2023, med ett belopp på 20 600 000 SEK.
We Effect samarbetar med two lokala partnerorganisationer; National Federation of Farmers (NFF), och Centre for Education and Development, Tearce (CED).
Det övergripande målet för programmet är att bidra till ökad sysselsättning och socio-ekonomisk makt över sin egen situation för människor som lever under marginaliserade förhållanden på landsbygden och i semiurbana miljöer. Resultaten på outcome-nivå är;
i) stärkta landsbygdsföretag och småskaliga bönder/producenter som genererar mer inkomst och ökar sysselsättningsgraden för människor på landsbygden, särskilt kvinnor och unga människor,
ii) mer motståndskraftiga och hållbara lokalsamhällen som främjar landsbygdsutveckling, särskilt för fattiga medlemmar inom de utvalda marknadssystemen,
iiii) fler romer har utvecklad kapacitet för, och tillgång till arbetsmarknaden, för att kunna ta anställning och utnyttja affärsmöjligheter inom de utvalda marknadssystemen,
iv) organisationsutveckling.
I dialogen mellan Sida, We Effect och dess partnerorganisationer kom parterna överens om att verka för en marknadsansats (Market Systems Development, MSD) i det nya programmet, IISEE.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement contribution 14097, Income Increase and Socio-Economic Empowerment, 2021-2023, North Macedonia
Support We Effect NMK Income Increase and Socio-Economic Empowerment 2021-2023

description.narrative:
Summary of Achieved Results (as of early 2026, incorporating latest data up to mid-2025)
The IISEE project delivered strong, impactful results using a Market Systems Development (MSD) approach, significantly improving socio-economic empowerment for small-scale farmers, rural communities (especially women and youth), and Roma job seekers in North Macedonia. By June 2025, the project reached 3,727 rights-holders (2,247 direct, 1,480 indirect; previous cumulative to end-2024: 3,423, meaning ~304 additional in early-mid 2025), with 47% women, achieving 90% of direct outreach targets. [Appendix 4 Results and Lessons Learnt from Phase I, p.3, Klaradia: UM2025/03667/SKOP-14] Beneficiaries gained new capabilities in market participation, formal employment, and resilient agribusiness changes previously limited by systemic barriers.
Key Expected Results
Income growth: Attributed gross income increase reached equivalent of 19.2 MSEK cumulatively by June 2025 (with potential long-term projection to 46.7 MSEK two years post-interventions). [Appendix 4, p.3,] Over 1,000 individuals saw ~55% average increase, driven by interventions in cereals, school schemes, and job matching. [Appendix 4, p.4,] Small-scale farmers (1,457 engaged cumulatively) transitioned to diversified models, e.g., contract farming and digital advisory services, enhancing revenues and formal market access. [Appendix 4, p.3]
Employment, especially Roma inclusion: 198 new jobs contracted cumulatively for Roma by June 2025 (44% women), with 148 retained for at least 6 months; 603 Roma accessed dedicated job-matching services. [Appendix 4, p.3] Key contributing activities in early 2025 included recording 34 new employments through the job-matching model implemented by Romalitico and the successful completion of vocational education and training (VET) for 95 unemployed Roma job seekers in high-demand sectors such as elderly care and photovoltaic installation (concluded in early April 2025). [Brief Progress Report Jan-Apr 2025, p.1, p.11, Klaradia: UM2023/26843/SKOP-245] These efforts supported Roma in gaining employable skills, confidence, and formal opportunities, reducing dependency on benefits while contributing to household stability and migration reduction. [Appendix 4, p.3,]
Market and community resilience: Farmers were offered improved products and services; Cooperatives like Sharri doubled membership (mostly women); initiatives like low-cost fencing was replicated by the National Park Shar Mountain in several other rural areas. Over 3,700 beneficiaries (direct/indirect) now have an increased income, access to new rural services, and economic independence. [Appendix 4, p.2, p.3,]
Sida assesses that the results achieved are broadly in line with expectations. The documented income growth, Roma employment outcomes, and strengthened market and cooperative structures demonstrate tangible progress toward increased economic inclusion and resilience. Continued institutional anchoring and market integration will be important to sustain these gains over time.
Unexpected/Positive Systemic Results
Beyond direct targets, the project triggered unanticipated systemic changes through replication, institutional uptake, and private-sector innovation, illustrating the MSD approachs catalytic potential.
For example, a low-cost fencing model piloted during potato harvesting intervention (to protect crops from wildlife) was replicated in 2025 by National Park Shar Mountain across several villages (e.g., Shipkovica, Bozovce, Veshala, and Vejce), demonstrating public-sector adoption of effective, low-tech solutions. [Appendix 4, p.2]
Institutional uptake included the annual Potato Day event (initiated under the project) receiving Ministry support in 2025, and groundwork for school schemes (piloted in 2022) influencing national priorities. [Appendix 4, p.2, also Brief Progress Report Jan-Apr 2025, p.1,2] One pilot partner moved from an informal small food operator to a fully registered company, gaining legitimacy, consumer trust, market access, and financial services, and serving as a role model for smallholder business formalisation. [Appendix 4, p.1]
Innovative models proved highly replicable: a new partnership with the Macedonian Association of Processors (MAP) introduced digital farming in value chains, improving supply chain efficiency; job-matching services scaled from textiles to manufacturing, creating pathways out of informality. [Appendix 4, p.2] Overall, the projected return on investment (~1.76 SEK per 1 SEK invested long-term) exceeded expectations, highlighting leveraged systemic impacts. [Appendix 4, p.3]
Sida assesses that the intervention has triggered positive systemic effects beyond its direct targets, including public-sector replication, institutional uptake, and private-sector formalisation. These developments indicate catalytic market changes and strengthened prospects for sustainable impact.
Notable Ongoing/Delayed Systemic Change
The project significantly influenced the draft Law on Agriculture and Rural Development (introducing Producer Organizations (PO)/Associations of POs; the definition of an active farmer; and school schemes alignment with EU CAP). [Appendix 4, p.1,2.] However, adoption remains pending as of early 2026 . The EU Commission country report for 2025 also flags that the CAP aligned framework is still missing and that it should be prioritized.
Overall, Sida assesses that the project made a clear difference: target groups shifted from vulnerability to resilience, with new behaviors (e.g., formal employment, diversified farming) and relations (stronger market linkages, community ownership). Sida also assesses that the programmes MSD approach yielded good results, confirming effectiveness amid challenges like policy delays. Sida assesses that to this date, Phase I outcomes provide a strong foundation for ongoing discussions for a potential second phase of the programme.
